_doc: settingAvailability() decides whether the Encrypted mode switch is operable
and, when it is not, WHICH sentence the user is told. It had no test of any
kind: the reason Dennis's standby session asserted 'Your phone app needs v58
or newer' about a phone that had never said anything is that peer.supports
was a BOOLEAN whose seed value was false, and false is the wire's word for
'the phone answered no'. Nothing pinned the difference, so nothing noticed.
TWO SURFACES, ONE DECISION. There is no Kotlin twin for this function — the
phone has no Encrypted-mode availability row — so RULE 30's 'both
implementations in one harness' is satisfied by the two WEB surfaces that do
and variant='menuitem' (the extension account menu). The suite reads that
component's SHIPPED source and proves both variants publish the same
reasonKey through data-cc-e2e-reason, so a surface that starts deciding for

availability.name: standby-unknown
availability.why: THE BUG. Phone in the lobby, no pair yet, capability never answered. Pre-fix this rendered peerTooOld.

availability.name: connected-unknown-pending
availability.why: lobbyState active but the accept has not published a capability answer yet. Same silence, same sentence.

availability.name: connected-supports-false
availability.why: The phone ANSWERED no — PAIRING_ACTIVE with no usable e2e block. The ONLY row allowed to claim a version gap.

availability.name: connected-supports-true
availability.why: A sealed pair with a usable block. The switch is operable and says nothing.

availability.name: key-mismatch
availability.why: TOFU key change outranks everything, including a phone that can do this.

availability.name: key-mismatch-outranks-no-phone
availability.why: CONTROL on the ORDER: keyChanged is checked before noPhone, so a mismatch survives the teardown that follows it.

availability.name: no-phone
availability.why: Nothing in the lobby. noPhone outranks the capability branches — unchanged by this lane.

availability.name: no-phone-outranks-supports-false
availability.why: CONTROL on the ORDER: a phone that answered no and then left is still 'connect your phone first'.

coherence.name: local-on-effective-off-active-pair
coherence.why: Screenshot 1. mode is the LOCAL pref (§12.2), so the switch shows ON and the repair notice explains why nothing changed on the latched pair.

coherence.name: local-on-effective-on
coherence.why: A pair that is already encrypting at the user's request. Switch ON, and NO notice: there is nothing to re-pair for.

coherence.name: standby-switch-reflects-pref-but-disabled
coherence.why: Standby. The switch still mirrors the LOCAL pref (it is a pref, not a status light) and is inoperable with peerUnknown.

indicator.name: verified-before-confirm
indicator.why: T-WEB-HEADER-VERIFIED-BEFORE-CONFIRM. The SAS dialog is OPEN. The header may not claim a code was confirmed before the user confirmed it.

indicator.name: verified-after-confirm
indicator.why: The user answered Matches. NOW the claim is true.

indicator.name: verified-no-sas-field
indicator.why: CONTROL: a caller that passes no sas object keeps the pre-lane behaviour exactly. Every existing vector row depends on this.

indicator.name: unencrypted-peer-answered-no
indicator.why: supports === false is an ANSWER, so naming the phone as the end that must update is honest here.

indicator.name: unencrypted-peer-unknown
indicator.why: Nobody answered, so the detail may NOT name the phone as the end at fault — the same rule as peerUnknown, on the other surface.

indicator.name: unencrypted-peer-supports
indicator.why: Both ends can, neither asked. Unchanged by this lane.
